key_insight: SoftServe turns quasi-Newton optimization into a scalable deep-learning method by constructing positive-definite curvature estimates that remain stable even under non-convexity and negative curvature.
engineering_relevance: It offers a GPU-friendly alternative to first-order optimizers for large, ill-conditioned models, with variants that scale to massive parameter counts without line searches or manual curvature fixes.
method: Derives curvature from the variational objective of Berglund et al. (2025) to keep updates positive definite.
Provides diagonal and Kronecker-factored SoftServe variants for large-scale neural networks.
Uses the coupled Newton-Schulz iteration to replace costly matrix decompositions with matrix multiplications.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong performance on severely ill-conditioned benchmarks, including recurrent networks, deep autoencoders, PINNs, and a 136M-parameter diffusion model, often outperforming Adam, Muon, and SOAP.
watch_item: Performance and stability may depend on careful implementation of the Newton-Schulz iteration and its numerical behavior at very large scale.
paper_title: SoftServe: A Scalable Quasi-Newton Method for Deep Learning
